feedback: Structural and semantic problems: (1) States u4 is unreachable — no transition enters u4 from any state, yet it carries transitions and rewards; dead states violate compactness/reachability. Likely intent: a path where the key is acquired before moving the blocker, but u0 only exits on `blocker_moved & !has_door_key`, so taking the key first (an allowed strategy per the environment, 149/300 episodes) falls into `else` self-loop and can never leave — the agent who picks up the key first is stuck with no path to door_open/target, yet could still reach target_picked_up in the environment; the RM must not dead-end a feasible solution. (2) Ordering regression on blocker_moved is partially handled (u1 -> u0 on `!blocker_moved`) but key regaining after key_lost lacks the blocker regression path: from u5, re-picking the key returns to u2 but a regression of blocker_moved (ball dropped back) is ignored everywhere — `blocker_moved` can turn false again and no transition handles it outside u1; the RM silently self-loops, giving no regression reward/signal where the task ('clear the ball... only then take the key') requires explicit regression handling at least in u2+ where key order matters. (3) In u2, simultaneous `key_lost` and `door_open` is impossible by constraints, fine; but in u2, if the agent still holds the key and opens the door, u3 correctly allows key drop (`else`), OK. (4) In u3/u4, `has_door_key` self-loops are fine, but `blocker_moved` regression in u3 (door open, ball dropped back) can't affect reachability — acceptable. (5) Reward safety: transition (u5, door_open) -> 0.05 gives door_open reward even without has_door_key in u5... actually u5 was entered via key_lost so key was once held; door_open there is legitimate but under-rewarded relative to u2->u3 (0.25 vs 0.05) — inconsistent but not unsafe. (6) Missing else self-loops are present in every state, good; event predicates (key_lost) are used as one-step triggers correctly. (7) Reward density: no reward for leaving the blocker-moved state, and u0->u1 requires `!has_door_key`, so an agent who moved the ball while holding the key... impossible (can't carry two). Acceptable in principle, but the dead/unreachable u4 and the key-first deadlock make the RM reject feasible solutions and mis-order credit. Rebuild with a key-first branch (u0 -> has_door_key state) and either remove u4 or make it reachable, and handle blocker_moved regression consistently in all pre-door states.
